title: First stint with Basie, replacing Jo Jones and Shadow Wilson
summary: Jo Jones recommended Gus; he joined Basie in late 1947, finished the Strand Theatre, then was displaced when Shadow Wilson returned.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: So you were with Cootie's small band before you went with Earl? Just for a brief time? Or Earl broke up at the Savoy and then you went with Cootie? Which?
I got with Cootie afterwards.
Yeah, yeah. So in other words, before
you joined Basie. What, Cootie? Yes.
Yeah.
Sure.
You were with Cootie.
Well, I had been with Basie, once.
How was that?

The first time I got with Basie, I stayed with him until -- and we went in the Strand Theatre. Now, that's -- I took Jo Jones' place after he took Shadow's place. And so he left and told them to get me to work with Basie.
Jo did.
Yes.
Yeah. Jo was always in your corner, wasn't he?
Well, yes.
Yeah.
And so I went to join Basie, like I said, in '47, see.
Yeah.

And -- the very last part of '47. I stayed with him until we went in the Strand Theatre, and I finished the Strand Theatre. Well, Shadow Wilson came back. He got -- he hired Shadow back into the band.
Yeah, yeah.
And they went in the Royal Roost, right across from the Strand.
Yeah.
And they stayed in there for about three weeks or a month, in the Royal Roost. Then they left and went out on the road.
Yeah.
And so, Jimmy Rushing told me, he said, 'Don't worry about it. I bet you Shadow won't be in the band a good month.' I said --
Did Shadow act up?
I don't know whether he acted up or not. When he left Basie the last time?
Why was it in and out?
Well, they had something going between themselves and so the office wanted Shadow back in the band, that's what it was.
I understand.

And they wanted him to play at the Strand Theatre. I told him no, he wasn't going to play the Strand. I was going to play the Strand Theatre. So his manager, Knowles, they used to call him, told him, -- said, 'Well, he's going to start tomorrow.' I said, 'If he's going to start tomorrow, he's going to have to whip me, and you, too.'

And Basie heard him, and Basie called him in there and told him, said, "He's going to finish this Strand Theatre. Now, you all want him to start over in the Royal Roost, okay, he starts after this job here." So I finished the Strand. And he came in the Royal Roost.

And so when they finished the job at the Royal Roost, they went out on the road. And they were out on the road a week, and he put his notice in and went and joined Woody Herman's band, Shadow. So Basie was left without a drummer. So he told Rushing to call me. And Rushing said, "No, I ain't going to call him." Said, "You didn't treat him right when he was here." And so they got Butch Ballard.
He's a white boy, isn't he?
No, no, Ballard, he played with Cootie Williams' band, too.
Oh, oh.
